title: Key transit routes
steps: KIX → Osaka Station/Shin-Osaka: JR Haruka limited express, ≈{{fact:haruka-kix-shin-osaka-1800-yen}}, direct from the airport terminal.
KIX → Namba: Nankai Rapi:t limited express, from ≈{{fact:nankai-rapit-kix-namba-700-yen}}, ~34 min minimum — the faster pick if your hotel sits on the Namba side of Osaka.
Osaka Station ↔ Kyoto Station: JR Special Rapid Service (Shin-Kaisoku), {{fact:jr-special-rapid-osaka-kyoto-580-yen}}, ~28–30 min, no transfer, roughly every 15 min.
Kyoto Station → Nara Station: JR Nara Line "Miyakoji Rapid", {{fact:jr-nara-line-kyoto-nara-720-yen}}, ~45 min, about every 30 min through the day.

Osaka-Namba → Kintetsu-Nara Station: Kintetsu Nara Line Limited Express, {{fact:kintetsu-nara-ltd-express-1200-yen}}, ~35–40 min; the non-limited-express Rapid/Express service covers the same route on the base ¥680 fare alone, a few minutes slower, no reservation.
Both Nara routes run every 15–30 min into the evening — the day trip is not a tight last-train connection; no need to build the day around a single return service.

title: IC card & rail passes
body:
ICOCA (JR West's IC card) is the right call for this trip — it taps onto every train, subway and bus used across Osaka, Kyoto and Nara, on both JR and non-JR (Kintetsu, Nankai) lines. Buy one at a KIX ticket machine on arrival.

Skip the multi-day rail passes for this itinerary. The Kansai Railway Pass Lite (formerly the Kansai Thru Pass) is sold Mar 25–Sep 30, 2026 and valid only Apr 1–Oct 2, 2026 for its 2026 edition — it does not cover this trip's Nov 13–17 dates at all, and it excludes JR lines (and the Kyoto City subway) entirely regardless. The JR West Kansai Area Pass (from ¥2,800/day) covers JR lines including the Haruka, but not the Kintetsu Nara Line used for the day trip — priced against this trip's actual mix of ~4 medium-length rides, pay-as-you-go ICOCA plus single Haruka tickets comes out roughly even or cheaper.
